html:
At Ponary, a forest outside Vilnius, German units and Lithuanian collaborators shot about 100,000 people from 1941 to 1944. Around 70,000 of them were Jews, most from Vilnius.

The killing began soon after Germany invaded in June 1941. Victims were brought to pits dug earlier for fuel tanks and shot. Poles, Soviet prisoners and others were also killed there. Late in the war prisoners were forced to dig up and burn the bodies to hide the crime.

About 95 percent of Lithuania's Jews were murdered in the Holocaust, among the highest shares in Europe. The world of the Vilna Gaon and of Yiddish Vilnius was destroyed. Under Soviet rule the Jewish identity of the victims was played down, and Lithuania's role is still debated.
sum: At Ponary, a forest outside Vilnius, German units and Lithuanian collaborators shot about 100,000 people from 1941 to 1944. Around 70,000 of them were Jews, most from Vilnius.
